$comment: Oxyn Pro items as metadata only (no code): the free build (no Pro sources overlaid) lists them with a Pro placeholder so the site, the search index and the registry index keep every item. Written by `node scripts/gen.mjs --write-pro-catalog` with the Pro sources overlaid; see CONTRIBUTING.md.

items.name: Comment thread
items.summary: One comment with replies – an assistant reports what it did, folds open details and answers @mentions.
keyboard: Reach the status line to fold its details open
a11y: Status lines are buttons with aria-expanded; the thread is a polite log that announces new replies.
responsive: Fills its container up to 420 px.

items.name: Comments panel
items.summary: Comment feed with filters, runnable /edit commands, resolve and a composer.
a11y: Filters are tabs, sorting is a menu of radio items, Resolve is a toggle button; the list announces new comments politely.
responsive: Fills its container up to 400 px; the list scrolls inside a 330 px cap with a thin pill thumb while the header, tabs and composer stay put.

items.name: AI answer
items.summary: Streamed answer with source cards, citation chips that preview their source, copy, regenerate, feedback and follow-ups.
keyboard: Source cards, citation chips, follow-ups, then the footer actions
a11y: The answer is a polite live region, busy while it streams; the status line reads Reading, Writing or Answer.
Citation chips are buttons named "Source: <titles>" and describe their tooltip (role=tooltip) while it is open.
Thumbs are toggle buttons (aria-pressed); thumbs down is aria-expanded over the reason chips; Copied and the thanks are announced.
responsive: Fills its container up to 640 px (480 in the demo); three source cards fit the row with a "+N" tile, two below 480 px, one below 340 px.

items.name: Cited answer
items.summary: An AI answer wired to its sources – point at a citation to light up its sentence and source, click to unfold the quoted passage with the matching words marked.
keyboard: Markers in reading order, then the source chips and Follow up
Unfold or fold that source's quote
a11y: Markers and chips are buttons named "Source 2: Cache Notes – Keeping build caches warm", aria-expanded and aria-controls on the quote.
The quote is a region named "Quote from <publication>"; the last row is a polite live region ("Quote copied").
The lit sentence changes weight as well as colour, so it reads without colour.
responsive: Fills its container up to 460 px and works from 300 px; below 400 px it tightens, below 360 px the number tags drop, below 280 px Copy quote keeps only its icon.

items.name: Message actions
items.summary: The quiet bar under an AI message – copy turns into a check, regenerate spins and unfolds a version switcher, thumbs pop and ask why, read aloud becomes a tiny equalizer.
keyboard: Copy, Regenerate, the version arrows, thumbs, Read aloud
a11y: The bar is a toolbar "Message actions"; thumbs and Read aloud are aria-pressed toggles, thumbs down is aria-expanded.
Versions read "Version 2 of 3"; a status region announces Copied, Regenerating, the vote and the thanks.
Tooltips are decoration (the buttons carry their names); the bar is never faded on touch screens.
responsive: Fills its container up to 544 px; touch screens get 36 px buttons, below 320 px Send wraps onto its own line.

items.name: Thinking pill
items.summary: A small working pill for AI replies – an eight-ray spinner and a shimmering label that rolls through phases and settles on a check.
a11y: role=status with aria-live=polite: each phase and the done label are read once.
The spinner, the check and the label rolling out are aria-hidden.
Reduced motion switches labels instantly and holds the spinner and shimmer still.
responsive: Sizes to its label on one line; keep phases to two to four words.

items.name: Thinking panel
items.summary: AI working panel with a live timer, searched sources and thinking steps that appear one by one.
keyboard: On the header: fold or unfold the steps; on "+N more": show every source
a11y: The header is one button with aria-expanded; the steps are an ordered list.
Source chips are links with their address as a tooltip; "+N more" is aria-expanded.
Reduced motion shows every step without animation.
responsive: Fills its container up to 420 px; chips wrap.

items.name: Writing assistant
items.summary: AI chat card with a soft gradient glow, suggestions, streaming replies and live voice dictation.
keyboard: Suggestions, the field, the mic, Send and New chat
a11y: New messages are announced politely; "Writing…" carries a label.
The mic is a toggle named Dictate / Stop dictation (aria-pressed).
responsive: Fills its container up to 380 px.

items.name: Findings feed
items.summary: A swarm of agents checking something – one calm row per agent with its progress, and their findings sliding into a short feed as they're found.
keyboard: The agents, then the findings in the feed
On an agent: only its findings (again: all); on a finding: open it
a11y: The feed is a polite live region: new findings are announced as they arrive.
Every severity has a text label for screen readers, not just a colour.
Agents are toggle buttons (aria-pressed) for the filter.
responsive: Below 480 px the check counts and locations drop so the rows keep one line.

items.name: Tool network
items.summary: Agents and the tools they call as a living network – a pulse along the link for every call and its answer, agents that breathe while they work and turn amber when they need you, and a card with each node's latest calls.
keyboard: Between the "needs you" / "failed" chips and the nodes; a focused node lights up its neighbourhood
Opens or closes the focused node's card
Closes the card and returns focus to its node
a11y: Every node is a button named with its name, kind, status, what it does and its calls in the last minute; aria-expanded says whether its card is open.
The card is a dialog; its close button takes focus, Esc closes it.
A visually hidden list gives the same picture as text: every node, its status, whom it called how often and its cost.
The chips sit in a polite live region; status is never colour alone – a badge and a line under the name.
responsive: The layout is computed for a wide and a narrow box with x as a share of the width, so it fits its container.
Below 520 px the graph turns taller than wide, nodes shrink, labels use short names and the card docks to the bottom.
Labels and the outer orbit stay inside the panel – nothing is cut off and nothing scrolls.

items.name: Relay trail
items.summary: A task passed from agent to agent like a relay – at every handoff what went along to the next one, what got lost on the way, and a light running down the line as the card drops in.
keyboard: Through the waiting tasks, the agents (while a task is picked up) and the handed-over items
Opens a card or an agent's task; on a lost item: shows why, and Add back
Drops a picked-up card, then closes what is open
a11y: Tasks can be given to an agent without dragging: double-click a card, then click an agent to its right.
Each column and each handoff's items are labelled lists; cards and lost items are buttons with aria-expanded.
Status is never colour alone: a spinner, a dot or a triangle beside the words.
responsive: Below about 760 px the status shows as an icon only.
Below 620 px the relay stacks into one column – an agent, its handoff, the next agent.
Cards keep their size; the columns fade out at the bottom instead of scrolling.

items.name: Task inbox
items.summary: All your background agent tasks in one calm list – live clocks and status tags, filter tabs with rolling counts, rows that unfold to the last steps with Approve, Reject, Retry or Open, and glide to their new place.
keyboard: The layout switch, then the cards and their buttons
a11y: Columns are labelled sections; cards are buttons with aria-expanded.
The layout switch is a radiogroup; a status line reads "2 need you, 2 running".
Status tags carry words as well as colour.
responsive: Fills its container up to 740 px; below 620 px the board stacks into one column.

items.name: Live lanes
items.summary: Where every agent is right now – a live timeline with a lane per agent, tasks growing into now, hand-offs drawn between agents and approvals right on the block.
keyboard: From block to block, lane by lane
Opens a block's summary, or the decision on a waiting one
Closes the decision or the summary
a11y: Every lane is a list labelled with the agent's name; every block is a button naming the agent, task, state and time.
A waiting block controls its decision (aria-expanded), a labelled dialog with Approve focused when you open it.
How many tasks need someone is announced politely when it changes.
responsive: Fills its container up to 760 px.
Below 520 px the names column shrinks to the avatars and every other tick label drops.

items.name: Change ledger
items.summary: Everything an agent changed in your systems, each change with an undo – before and after per row, and pointing at Undo shows what would go with it and what can't be taken back.
keyboard: Moves through Undo and Redo; focusing Undo shows what goes with it
Undoes or redoes the focused change
a11y: An ordered list named after the ledger, latest entry on top.
Undo is named with the change and how many build on it; Redo with the change.
Before → after is plain text and the arrow is read as "to"; what was undone is announced.
responsive: 640 px up to its container.
Below 480 px the system name drops and Undo / Redo shrink to round icon buttons.
On touch screens Undo and Redo show on every row in place of the time.

items.name: Run monitor
items.summary: One agent at work as a card – the current step with a clock and the bill so far, a time strip, the finished steps with each tool's logo, the exact command when it needs an OK, and a fold into a small bar.
keyboard: Fold away, the finished steps, then the controls in the foot
While it waits and the card has focus: Allow
While it waits: Decline; with step details open, closes them
On a step: opens its details (focus moves to Close)
a11y: The card is a region named with the agent, its state and the current step; folded, the bar is one button with the same name.
The time strip is one image labelled with every step and its time; finished steps are a list of buttons with aria-expanded.
A step's details are a labelled dialog; the ask is announced when the card starts waiting.
responsive: A 340 px card that shrinks with its container; labels and the command ellipsize.

items.name: Job queue
items.summary: The work waiting for your agents and how fast it moves – a live queue, workers running jobs as growing bars, Done and Failed, and a depth chart that shows the backlog build up under a rate limit and drain after.
keyboard: Into the jobs (the front job is the one stop), then the card's buttons
Opens or closes the focused job's card
a11y: Every job is a button named with its kind, how long it waited or ran, its place in line, priority and attempt.
Pause is a toggle with aria-pressed; the stepper's buttons say what they do and the count is announced.
The chart is an image summarised in words; rate limits, pauses and crossing the backpressure line are announced politely.
responsive: 756 px up to its container.
Under 600 px the flow stacks and the four numbers wrap to two columns; under 440 px Pause and the stepper get their own row.

items.name: Overnight recap
items.summary: A catch-up card for when you come back: a tiny timeline of the night with a spike per event, then grouped items – waiting on you, broken, finished – each with its action in place.
keyboard: Through each card's buttons, lane by lane; focusing a card lights its dot
Runs the focused action, Undo or Redo
a11y: Each lane is a labelled section with its cards as a list; the chart is decorative and the summary says the counts in words.
While an action works its buttons are disabled and the row says Working…; the result and every undo are announced.
State is never colour alone: lanes are named, tags say Done, Approved, Fixed or Undone.
responsive: 804 px up to its container.
Under 640 px the three lanes stack and stop reserving room for three cards.

items.name: Sequence diagram
items.summary: One agent run as a sequence diagram – a column for you, each agent and each tool, every message an arrow between lifelines, calls solid and replies dashed, bars while a participant works, and parallel or retried messages in labelled frames.
keyboard: To the participant chips, then into the message list
Opens the focused participant's or message's card
a11y: Messages are an ordered list; each is named "Sender to Receiver: text, status, m:ss" and says it opens a dialog.
Participants are buttons; cards are dialogs with a close button you can reach by Tab.
Colour never carries meaning alone: replies are dashed, failures say so and carry a cross, frames are labelled.
responsive: 800 px up to its container; the columns share the width.
Under 560 px the chips show only their marks and the time gutter and times shrink.

items.name: Return brief
items.summary: The While you were away card for a chat thread – how long you were gone, what needs you, what failed and what's done as a short list with one action per row; Got it folds it into a one-line divider.
keyboard: Through the row actions, then Show more and Got it
Runs the focused action; Got it folds the card and focuses the divider, which opens it again
Folds the card from anywhere inside it
a11y: A region named While you were away with a heading that says how long; the rows are a list.
Every action names its task ("Decide: Export job") and each row says its state in words.
Got it and the divider are buttons with aria-expanded; a working button stays focusable (aria-disabled); changes are announced politely.
responsive: 600 px up to its container; rows keep one height in every state.
Under 460 px the counts drop under the title; titles, details and long action labels end in an ellipsis.

items.name: Attempt race
items.summary: One task tried several ways at once: every attempt races as a row with its model, approach and a live bar, finishes with a score, and the best one is marked and used – switch to another if you prefer.
keyboard: Moves between the finished attempts' Use buttons
a11y: The rows form a radiogroup labelled by the heading; a finished attempt's Use control is a radio whose name gives the model and its score.
Bars are decorative; progress, failure and score are all in text.
Reduced motion drops the stagger, the shine and the glides.
responsive: Wide: tile, name and approach, bar, score and the use button in one line.
Under 560 px the bar goes under the name, the approach and the task drop out.

items.name: Memory panel
items.summary: What the assistant remembers about you, by category: filter or search it, pause a memory, edit or forget it with a short undo, add your own, or switch memory off without losing anything.
keyboard: Switch, chips, search, each memory's actions, New memory
Saves an edit or a new memory (Shift+Enter: new line)
Cancels an edit, the new memory or the search
a11y: Use memory is a role=switch; the chips are a radiogroup with roving focus; Pause is a toggle (aria-pressed).
Each row's actions also appear on keyboard focus, not only on hover.
Saves, pauses, forgets and undos are read out by a polite status region.
responsive: A narrow card (320 px, shrinks with its container); the chip row scrolls sideways instead of wrapping.
Past 360 px the rows scroll within the card.

items.name: Activity pill
items.summary: A compact pill for an app bar or side rail counting background agent work – how much is running, how much waits on you – that opens to each task's ring, current step, Pause / Resume and Open.
keyboard: Opens or closes the list from the pill
Each task, its Pause / Resume or Open, then Open tasks
a11y: The pill is a popup button (aria-expanded) whose name carries the counts; the list is a labelled dialog.
Each row's main button names the task and its step; Pause and Resume are named per task.
Finishing tasks are read out politely; reduced motion stops the ring sweep.
responsive: The pill is inline and fits any header; the 284 px list opens below and aligned to the pill's end, or to the right in a sidebar.

items.name: Plan vs actual
items.summary: How an agent's run is going against its plan: each step's real bar over a dashed planned one, overruns in amber, later steps pushed right and the expected finish drifting from the planned finish.
keyboard: Selects a step to show its links and cost
a11y: Each step is a toggle button whose name says how long it took against plan, or when it is expected to start.
The header status (behind / ahead / on plan) is a status region; the chart marks are aria-hidden.
Overruns are named in text (+14s), never by colour alone; reduced motion stops the sheen, spin and glides.
responsive: Rows keep their 28 px height at every width; the bars share the space after the 150 px name column.
Under 560 px the name column narrows to 96 px and the task, glyphs and axis labels drop out.

items.name: Root cause tree
items.summary: Why a run failed, drawn as a fault tree: guesses under OR and AND gates are checked one at a time and ruled out or confirmed, the confirmed route to the failure is highlighted, and any node opens its verdict and evidence.
keyboard: Into the tree, then the evidence buttons
Previous or next node, depth first
The failure, or the last hypothesis
a11y: The tree is role=tree; every node is a treeitem button with its level, selection and status in its name.
Status is always in words (Ruled out, Confirmed, Root cause), never colour alone; the counts are a status region.
Reduced motion stops the spinner, the fades and the scale-in.
responsive: Wide: a top-down tree, cards 124 px, gates between levels and elbows joining siblings.
Under 600 px: an indented outline, full-width cards, the evidence below.

items.name: Load planner
items.summary: When agent runs happen across a day, drawn as the token load against an API's per-minute limit: drag a run's bar to move it, spread the runs out to lower the peak, and get the nearest start that keeps a run under the limit.
keyboard: Moves through the runs, their bars and buttons
Selects a run or presses a button
Closes the edit window, then clears the selection
a11y: Each bar is a slider whose value text is its start time; a run already under way is a disabled slider.
The pill (under, close to or over the limit) is a status region; the chart is aria-hidden and the footer says the same in words.
Over the limit is named in text with its times, never by the red hatching alone.
responsive: Rows keep 28 px; bars share the width after the name and time columns.
Under 520 px the name column narrows, the axis keeps every other label and the now label drops out.

items.name: Assign board
items.summary: Hand tasks to agents yourself: a pile of unassigned work beside each agent's model, rate, busy-until time and queue, with the money waiting in queues – or switch on Auto and let whoever frees up first take the next one.
keyboard: Picks up the focused task; Enter again hands it to the chosen agent
Chooses the agent while a task is held
Hands the held task to that agent at once
a11y: Pile cards are toggle buttons (aria-pressed while held); each agent is a named group whose digit button carries aria-keyshortcuts.
Auto is a role=switch; each hand-over and put-back is read out by a polite status region.
Dragging is optional – Enter, the arrows and the digits do the same; the +N chip is focusable and lists the rest in a tooltip.
responsive: Fills up to 720 px: pile left (170 px), agents right.
Under 560 px the pile sits above the agents and the hint line drops out of the header.

items.name: Dictation button
items.summary: Speech to text in the field: a mic that listens, interim words in grey that settle when final, inserted at the caret, with cancel and an error state.
keyboard: Cancel and drop the interim words
a11y: The mic button is named for its action: “Dictate” or “Stop dictation”.
Interim words are aria-hidden; a polite region announces listening, done and cancel.
responsive: The field grows to its container; the mic never wraps.

items.name: Mention input
items.summary: Type @ to mention people, files and agents or / for commands: ranked, grouped suggestions at the caret, keyboard picking, and pills for accepted mentions.
keyboard: Send when the list is closed
a11y: The field is a combobox with aria-activedescendant on the open listbox.
Options carry aria-selected; a polite region announces the result count.
responsive: The list matches the field width, capped at 360 px.

items.name: Mode switch
items.summary: Switch the agent between Ask, Plan and Agent: segmented or as a menu, a placeholder that follows the mode, and a change that waits for the next turn while it runs.
a11y: Segments are a radiogroup with aria-checked; the menu is a listbox.
A queued change is announced: “Plan from the next turn”.
responsive: Use the menu variant where the segments do not fit.

items.name: Permission selector
items.summary: How much the agent may do without asking: Read only, Ask before edits, Auto-edit or Full access, with risk levels, a confirm for full access and a workspace ceiling.
keyboard: Open the presets or choose one
a11y: Presets are a radiogroup; blocked ones are aria-disabled with the reason.
Full access asks in an alertdialog before it applies.
responsive: Cards wrap to one column in narrow frames.

items.name: Tools menu
items.summary: Choose which tools the agent may use: grouped switches, group toggles, a filter, and connectors that ask you to sign in first.
a11y: Each tool is a switch (role switch, aria-checked); groups are labelled.
Group buttons read “Turn all on” or “Turn all off”; changes are announced politely.
responsive: The menu scrolls past 360 px of height.

items.name: Agent steering
items.summary: Guide a running agent without stopping it: notes queue for its next step and show when picked up, or interrupt the current step.
keyboard: Send a note at the next step
a11y: The current step is a status region; picked-up notes are announced.
Interrupt is a toggle (aria-pressed).
responsive: The step line truncates; the note field keeps its width.

items.name: Sidebar
items.summary: An app sidebar: brand, sections with nested groups, pinned pages, settings and the account; folds to an icon rail.
keyboard: Open a row or toggle a group
a11y: A labelled nav; the open page has aria-current.
Groups expose aria-expanded; rail rows carry the label and unread count.
Fold and expand are announced politely.
responsive: The frame fills the stage width; the sidebar keeps its width and the content column takes the rest.
Below 640 px fold the sidebar to the rail with `[`.

items.name: Sidebar rail
items.summary: A resizable sidebar that snaps to a 64 px icon rail, with a keyboard splitter and a breadcrumb that follows the page.
keyboard: Resize by 16 px on the separator
a11y: The separator is a focusable splitter with value and text.
The breadcrumb follows the open page.
responsive: The frame fills the stage width; the sidebar keeps its width and the content column takes the rest.
Below 640 px fold the sidebar to the rail with `[`.

items.name: Inbox sidebar
items.summary: Mail folders with counts and labels beside a message list: drag onto folders or Move to, star, archive, undo, and a Compose button that grows into a composer.
a11y: Folder rows name their unread counts.
Each message row reads sender, subject, time and state.
Moves, stars and undo are announced.
responsive: The frame fills the stage width; the sidebar keeps its width and the content column takes the rest.
Below 640 px fold the sidebar to the rail with `[`.

items.name: App shell
items.summary: The app frame: sidebar, header with title and actions, and content, flat or inset.
a11y: Landmarks: nav, header, main content.
Header actions are labelled icon buttons.
responsive: The frame fills the stage width; the sidebar keeps its width and the content column takes the rest.
Below 640 px fold the sidebar to the rail with `[`.

items.name: AI side panel
items.summary: An assistant docked beside a page: it streams an answer, proposes an edit as a word diff, applies it with a tint and offers Undo.
a11y: The panel is a labelled complementary region; the thread is a polite log.
Apply moves focus to Undo; changes are announced.
responsive: The panel takes up to 48% of the frame and at most 340 px.

items.name: Terminal tabs
items.summary: Terminal tabs: add, close, rename, cycle with Ctrl+Tab, activity dots on background tabs and exit codes.
a11y: A tablist with one tabpanel; background output adds “new output” to the tab name.
Close buttons are labelled per tab.
responsive: The strip scrolls sideways when tabs overflow.

items.name: Sidebar Nav
items.summary: Grouped sidebar links with a sliding active indicator, collapsible groups and badges.
keyboard: Open a link or toggle a group
a11y: Links carry aria-current; group headings expose aria-expanded.
responsive: Fixed 240 px column.

items.name: Harness
items.summary: A demo frame with viewport widths, a dark canvas and a Fork this button that hands over the current demo and its settings.
a11y: The viewport switch is a radio group.
Fork this announces the fork politely.
responsive: Phone and tablet widths clamp to the stage.

items.name: AI Chat screens
items.summary: The seven AI Chat screens (Start, Overview, Agents, Double sidebar, Progress, Run, Agent thread) composed from the chat, composer, plan, tool and approval parts.
keyboard: Rail, threads, main column, side panel
a11y: Each screen has nav, main and complementary landmarks.
Streamed answers announce politely; approvals keep their own keys.
responsive: The side panel and thread list keep fixed widths; the main column flexes.

items.name: Status indicator
items.summary: A dot and a label for any of the 13 agent states, as a pill, inline or a dot alone; the verb comes from a verb pack and stalls show how long.
a11y: role=status with aria-live=polite, so state changes are announced.
The dot variant keeps the label as its accessible name.
The pulse is removed under prefers-reduced-motion.
responsive: small (6 px dot, 12 px text) for dense rows; medium (8 px, 13 px) elsewhere.

items.name: Tool stack
items.summary: A turn's tool calls grouped the way a transcript reads them: runs of reads fold into one line, parallel calls show live, and a finished turn folds into "Worked for 31s".
keyboard: Close / open a group row (tree semantics)
a11y: Group rows use tree semantics (treeitem, ← / →); each call row is a button with aria-expanded.
responsive: Groups keep long turns short; density trades detail for space.

items.name: Todo list
items.summary: The agent's task list: done, active, blocked, pending and skipped items, as a checklist or a dock above the composer that fades once everything is done.
a11y: role=list labelled "Agent tasks, 2 of 6 done"; each item reads its label, status and duration.
An item becoming active is announced only if it stays active for 2 s.
responsive: checklist fills a panel; dock sits above the composer and expands on demand.

items.name: Step timeline
items.summary: The plan as a vertical timeline, each step with its time and the tool calls it made; folds to one line once every step is done.
keyboard: Open a folded timeline or a step's calls
a11y: An ordered list; nested calls are a sub-list.
responsive: Fills its container; fold_on_done keeps finished plans to one line.

items.name: Plan card
items.summary: A plan as a document you review before the agent runs it: drafting, proposed with Approve or Build, executing, or superseded by a newer version.
a11y: role=region labelled with the plan title and version.
responsive: Fills its container.

items.name: Approval pager
items.summary: Several open requests in one card: page through them with ‹ › and allow the whole batch once.
keyboard: Through the pager and the decision buttons
a11y: The pager text ("1 of 3") and the batch row are real text next to the card's buttons.
responsive: Fills its container; the batch row stays under the card.

items.name: Decision card
items.summary: An agent's question in its own card above the composer: numbered options with one Recommended, tiles for a pick, Approve / Decline with facts, or your own words.
keyboard: Answer with that row at once; the next number goes into the field
Move between rows; ↓ from the last row goes into the field
Answer with the focused row; in the field Enter sends your words
Later: fold the card to one line
a11y: The card is a group named by the question; rows are a listbox with one tab stop.
Each row says its number key (aria-keyshortcuts); Later says Escape.
Answers and Later are announced politely with how many still wait.
responsive: Takes the composer's width; long titles wrap to two lines then end in ….
Below 420 px tiles turn into rows; touch rows are 44 px.

items.name: Approval questions
items.summary: Paged questions the agent asks before acting: an odometer counter, single choice that moves on by itself, multi-select, your own answer, Skip and Send.
keyboard: Pick; single choice moves on after 480 ms
a11y: Single choice is a radiogroup, multi-select a group of checkboxes; the counter is named “Question 1 of 3”.
The card is aria-live=polite so each new question is read.
Prev, Next and Dismiss are labelled icon buttons.
responsive: Fills its container up to 460 px; option rows wrap their text.

items.name: Hold to confirm
items.summary: Confirm a destructive action by holding, not tapping: the fill runs while held, rewinds smoothly when you let go early and resumes from where it was on a quick re-press; a check draws in when done.
keyboard: Fills the button; releasing early rewinds it
a11y: A real button named “… hold to confirm”; the hint below is its description and a polite live region (“Keep holding…”, “Done”).
The check is drawn in after completion; the label changes to the confirmed label.
responsive: Inline size; touch-action none so a hold never scrolls the page.

items.name: Inline confirm
items.summary: A destructive button that morphs into an inline question, a spinner and a result with Undo, or an error with Retry. Confirm by press, by hold, or with a countdown Escape can still stop.
keyboard: Cancel the question or stop the countdown
a11y: One group; every face keeps a real button so focus never drops to the page.
Each change (asking, deleting, deleted, error) is announced in a polite live region.
responsive: Grows inline from the resting button; the question never wraps.

items.name: Approval gates
items.summary: Every approval request of a run as a stack: the one to decide now on top with who asks, what exactly and why, its input or diff; approve, change it first or reject, and it drops into the Decided list while the next rises. Open gates say how many steps they hold.
a11y: A section named Approvals; the waiting count and held steps are text in the header.

items.name: Expanding search
items.summary: An icon that morphs into a search field with grouped, highlighted results beneath; the panel tracks the field's width; Enter picks and folds it back.
a11y: Combobox with aria-activedescendant over a listbox of labelled groups.
Counts and empty states are announced; the folded field is not in the tab order.
responsive: Grows to the smaller of its width and its container; the panel caps at min(22 rem, 60 vh).

items.name: Shortcut recorder
items.summary: Record a key combination into caps: held modifiers show as you build it, reserved and taken shortcuts ask first, plus a searchable cheatsheet that lights held keys.
a11y: A button with aria-pressed while recording, named by the label and the spoken shortcut.
Conflicts offer Use anyway and Cancel as real buttons; results are announced.
responsive: The cheatsheet goes two columns from 520 px.

items.name: Pagination
items.summary: Previous and next around a sliding five-page window with a travelling current mark; numbers slide like a belt when the window shifts. Oxyn adds ellipsis, cursor, load-more and page sizes.
a11y: A nav landmark; the current page has aria-current=page; previous and next are disabled at the ends.
responsive: Window mode keeps the same width on any screen; the row wraps when it must.

items.name: Thinking
items.summary: Steps, reasoning, search and coding rows playing in with pending, active, done and failed marks.
a11y: Each row's mark carries its status as a label.
The header is a disclosure button with aria-expanded.
responsive: Details ellipsize; rows never wrap their mark.

items.name: Source cards
items.summary: Cited sources under an answer: cards stream into reserved slots, the overflow becomes a favicon stack, hover previews the snippet and citations highlight their card.
keyboard: Open a card or the stack
a11y: A labelled list, aria-busy while searching; skeletons are hidden.
Each card reads number, title and domain, and says it opens a new tab.
A polite region announces the status once.
responsive: max + 1 columns; two below 540 px of container.

items.name: Starter prompts
items.summary: The empty state of an AI app: a greeting, starter cards by category with a staggered shuffle, and a composer the cards fill.
keyboard: Fill the composer from a card
a11y: A labelled section with the greeting as its heading.
Card names include title, app and category.
Picks and shuffles are announced politely.
responsive: Two columns; one below 480 px of container.

items.name: AI chat
items.summary: A full AI chat block: a user turn, the assistant thinking, searching and streaming a cited answer, then actions.
keyboard: Through the transcript to the composer
a11y: The transcript is a polite log; each turn is an article.
responsive: Fills its container up to 760 px.

items.name: Document extraction
items.summary: Fields pulled from a document with confidence and page provenance: hover a field to see where it came from, review the low-confidence ones, then confirm.
a11y: Confidence has a label in percent, not just a bar.
Fields are labelled inputs with their page.
responsive: Document and fields stack below 620 px of container.

items.name: Research run
items.summary: A deep-research job: phases, the queries it ran, sources rolling in, progress and elapsed time, ending on a report.
a11y: A progressbar with a value; the current phase has aria-current=step.
responsive: Columns stack below 520 px of container.

items.name: Support conversation
items.summary: A support chat that starts with an AI assistant, hands off to a person with a queue position, and ends with a rating.
a11y: The transcript is a polite log; the banner states who is answering.
responsive: Up to 560 px.

items.name: Recommendation card
items.summary: A suggestion with its reason, confidence, impact and evidence, accepted or dismissed with Undo.
a11y: Confidence is text; the decision is announced as status.
responsive: Up to 440 px.

items.name: Context cards
items.summary: What the agent used, with kind icons and token cost; pin to keep, remove to drop.
a11y: Pin is a toggle (aria-pressed); remove names its card.
responsive: Columns of at least 210 px; one column in narrow frames.

items.name: Breadcrumb
items.summary: Where a page sits: links from the root to the current page, new crumbs sliding in from a blur, and an optional “…” that folds the middle.
keyboard: Follow the focused crumb or reveal hidden ones
a11y: nav landmark with an ordered list.
The last item has aria-current=page and is never a link.
Separators are aria-hidden.
responsive: Wraps onto new lines; crumbs never wrap inside.
Use max to collapse long paths on narrow screens.

items.name: Accordion
items.summary: Supporting detail revealed in place: the panel height grows while the answer slides down out of a blur, the chevron springs.
a11y: Triggers sit in h3 with aria-expanded and aria-controls.
Panels are labelled regions and become visibility:hidden once closed.
responsive: Rows fill the width; lg caps answers at 62ch and tightens below 520px.

items.name: Resizable panels
items.summary: Trade space between panes by dragging or with the keyboard: rubber-band limits, squeezed content fades, collapsible panes leave a restore tab.
a11y: Dividers are focusable separators with aria-valuenow, min, max and valuetext.
Collapsed panes are inert; the group is labelled.
responsive: Needs a definite height; panes do not stack on mobile (switch to tabs).
Pointer capture with touch-action none for touch, pen and mouse.

items.name: Drawer
items.summary: A temporary side surface built on the sheet: titled header that doubles as the drag handle, flick or drag past a third to close, any edge.
keyboard: Close and return focus to the trigger
a11y: role=dialog with aria-modal, title and description wired.
Close button labelled; dragging is never the only way to close.
responsive: Side drawers cap at the window width minus a gutter; top / bottom span the width.

items.name: Tree view
items.summary: Nested folders with keyboard navigation, rows that stagger in when a folder opens, guide lines and git or agent status badges.
keyboard: Open a folder, then into it
Close a folder, then to its parent
a11y: tree / treeitem with aria-level, posinset, setsize, expanded and selected.
Roving tabindex; icons, chevrons and guides are aria-hidden.
responsive: 36 px rows (28 compact), labels ellipsize, 18 px per level.

items.name: Table of contents progress
items.summary: Contents that read along with you: a line fills through the headings, a marker rides to the current section and the time left rolls down to Finished.
keyboard: Scroll the article to the heading
a11y: nav landmark named by the title, an ordered list of anchor links.
aria-current=location on the current heading; contrast differs, not only the line.
The line and marker are decorative.
responsive: Below 560px of container width the contents move above the article.

items.name: Page header
items.summary: A project header that folds into a compact bar as the page scrolls, with breadcrumb, actions and tabs whose counts roll.
a11y: Tabs use tab roles; the current crumb carries aria-current.
The icon-only actions trigger is labelled More actions.
Follow, Share, Copy link and Archive report through a polite status region.
responsive: Action labels hide in the folded bar and in narrow containers.

items.name: Dock
items.summary: A floating tool dock: a label glides between items, a tint springs to the chosen tool, groups grow a tray and items reorder with Alt + arrows.
keyboard: Along the dock (or inside a tray)
Choose; on a group, toggle its tray
a11y: toolbar with roving tabindex; plain items use aria-pressed.
Groups have aria-haspopup, aria-expanded and aria-controls; closed trays are inert.
Names include the shortcut and badge (“Pen, P”).
responsive: The floating label shows on hover and focus, not touch.

items.name: Expandable text
items.summary: Long text clamped to a few lines with a soft fade; Read more glides open, Show less closes, and the toggle only appears when the text overflows.
keyboard: Open or close from the toggle
a11y: The clamp is visual: the whole text stays in the accessibility tree.
The toggle has aria-expanded and aria-controls; labels crossfade in one cell.
responsive: The clamp is plain CSS, so width and font changes need no script.

items.name: Toggle group
items.summary: A row of toggles, single or multiple: one fill glides between options, or each fades in and neighbours join like a formatting toolbar.
keyboard: In and out on one item
a11y: Single: radiogroup with radios and aria-checked. Multiple: group with aria-pressed.
Icon-only items take their name and tooltip from label.
responsive: Stays on one line; md items are 36 px for touch.

items.name: Chip group
items.summary: Filter chips that morph as you pick them: a check grows in, the label slides, long sets fold behind +N more and selected chips never hide.
a11y: group with aria-label; chips are buttons with aria-pressed.
Selected chips always stay visible.
responsive: Chips wrap onto new lines.

items.name: Radio cards
items.summary: Option cards that need more than a label: one ring glides to the selected card, price and description slots, radio keyboard behaviour.
keyboard: Select the next enabled card, wrapping
a11y: radiogroup / radio with aria-checked and aria-disabled; described by description or the disabled reason.
Selection shows a ring and a filled dot, not colour alone.
responsive: auto-fill columns down to one in narrow containers.

items.name: Rating
items.summary: Capture a numeric opinion: stars as a radio group with half steps, scrubbing, clearing and a value word that rolls.
a11y: radiogroup with one radio per step labelled “Great, 4 of 5 stars”; commits announced politely.
Read-only renders role=img with an aria-label.
responsive: 36 px touch cells; the word wraps under the stars when space runs out.

items.name: Reorderable list
items.summary: Reorder by dragging the grip or with arrow keys: rows lift, neighbours slide and the position number rolls.
a11y: Handles are labelled “Reorder X. Position 1 of 4. Use arrow keys.”
Focus stays on the moved handle; moves are announced.
responsive: Only the grip starts a drag (touch-action none), so rows still scroll the page.

items.name: Reactions
items.summary: Acknowledge in one tap: reaction pills whose counts roll, your own highlighted, and a picker tray that grows out of the add button.
keyboard: Toggle a pill or open the picker
a11y: group of buttons with aria-pressed and labels like “Love, 4 reactions, including yours”.
The picker is a labelled toolbar; changes are announced.
responsive: Pills wrap; the tray grows out of the add button.

items.name: User menu
items.summary: Your account behind the avatar: identity, a few links, an inline theme and status switch that keep the menu open, usage, and sign out with a spinner.
a11y: Trigger has aria-haspopup=menu, aria-expanded and “Account menu, name, status”.
Rows are menuitems; switches are menuitemradio groups.
Sign out sets aria-busy while it runs.
responsive: Below 640px the panel becomes a bottom sheet.

items.name: Team switcher
items.summary: A workspace switcher like Linear or Slack: the current tile and plan, search, roles, ⌘1–9, inline create and join, and a shimmering switch.
keyboard: Filter by name, plan or role
a11y: Trigger: aria-haspopup=dialog, aria-expanded, aria-busy while switching.
Search is a combobox with aria-activedescendant; the current workspace is aria-selected with a check.
A polite region announces switches.
responsive: The panel caps at the viewport minus a gutter.

items.name: Notification center
items.summary: A home for updates: unread badge, All and Unread views, grouped rows that expand in place, mark all read and clear, with a bell that tilts.
keyboard: Rows, dismiss buttons, views and bulk actions
a11y: The bell label includes the unread count; the badge is aria-hidden.
Rows use aria-expanded; focus moves to the next row after a dismiss.
The summary line is polite.
responsive: The panel caps at the viewport minus a gutter.

items.name: Hover card
items.summary: Preview a person, agent or source on hover or focus: a short delay, a grace period while you travel into it, and a fast warm re-open.
keyboard: Focus opens the card at once
Close and stay closed while hovering
a11y: role=tooltip; the trigger gets aria-describedby while open.
Focus never moves into the card.
responsive: 18.5rem wide, capped to the viewport; taps toggle on touch.

items.name: Empty states
items.summary: A useful next step when there is nothing to show: first run, no results, no runs, inbox zero, offline, error and no access.
a11y: role=status with a title; the icon is aria-hidden.
Copy changes roll in place.
responsive: Centred up to 520px.
